To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ps-width of CNF formulas is a useful structural parameter for MaxSAT and # SAT and that the ps-width is bounded for some classes of CNF formulas that do not have bounded branch-width.
for some classes of CNF formulas the weighted MaxSAT and \#SAT problems can be solved in time polynomial in the size of the formula.
we define a structural parameter of Boolean formulas and use it as a tool for identifying instances of weighted MaxSat and #Sat that can be solved polynomial time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: What kind of structure in CNF formulas allows us to solve weighted MaxSAT and \#SAT efficiently?
structural parameters of CNF formulas, and how to use them to design algorithms for weighted MaxSAT and \(\#\)SAT.
structural properties of CNF formulas that can be used to identify classes of CNF formulas for which weighted MaxSAT and/or #SAT can be solved in \({\mathscr P}\).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have a new structural parameter of CNFs, the ps-width.
the ps-width is a new parameter that is a natural and powerful generalization of the treewidth and the cliquewidth.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for some graph classes, we can solve weighted MaxSAT in polynomial time, even though we do not have a bound on the size of the largest clique in the graph, and even though the graph does not have bounded clique width.
we can solve weighted MaxSAT and \({\#}\hbox {SAT}\) on formulas with polynomial ps-width in time polynomial in the total size of the formula.
the ps-width is a new structural parameter for CNF formulas and that the ps-width of some classes of formulas is polynomially bounded.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for some classes of CNF formulas, the ps-width is a better measure of tractability than the clique-width.
